EXIMROUTES.why: Slightly above the ₹88 issue price after listing 19 December 2025 at a 25% premium, then fell through 2026 (₹150 in April, ₹107 in August; 52-week range ₹104.50-281.90). The sources do not say why. FY26 revenue was ₹207 crore (+72%) from volume growth; ROE 33.6%. It is a platform for recycled paper imports.
EXIMROUTES.outlook: Management targets 30-50% revenue growth in FY27 (up to ₹300 crore) and a ₹1,000 crore business in five years with 8-10% of India's recycled-paper imports. These are company targets. P/E fell from about 42 in April to about 20 in August.

NOVUS.why: Up about 40% on the ₹146 issue price, with a 45% gain in six months to about ₹204 (22 September 2026); ₹144 in early August. IPO ran 17-20 March 2026, listed on BSE SME 25 March. Profit grew to about ₹9.3 crore in FY26 from ₹3.0 crore in FY24 with no borrowings. No source gave a cause for the run. Offer-document risks: dependence on few customers, data security, and unidentified acquisition targets.
NOVUS.outlook: No analyst forecast or guidance found. The product roadmap includes AI features and cloud migration. Reported P/E is shown as 0 (low EPS base) and price-to-book 3.6-5.2.

EMIAC.why: Slightly below the ₹98 issue price after listing at ₹107.80 (+10%) on a 3.2x subscribed IPO; it drifted to about ₹92 by mid-August 2026 (52-week range ₹89-121). FY26 revenue rose 63% to ₹32.3 crore, but net margin fell to 11.2% from 21.2%, and reports on profit growth conflict (+14.5% vs lower). It runs AI-driven digital marketing.
EMIAC.outlook: No analyst coverage or guidance found. Thin liquidity and a small float are risks; price-to-book is high (2.6-12.5 by source).

UHMVL.why: Down about 81% from the ₹166 issue price. It listed on 11 June 2026 about 20% below the issue price (₹126.20 lower circuit) on a weakly subscribed IPO (about 2.3x; non-institutional 0.9x) priced at a 'pricey' valuation, then kept falling: ₹93 in late June, ₹36 on 22 July, ₹30.60 on 18 September. Margin pressure from competition in travel aggregation was flagged. FY26 revenue rose to ₹37.5 crore but profit fell to ₹1.56 crore from ₹2.66 crore.
UHMVL.outlook: No analyst targets or company guidance found. No specific event explained the decline after listing; the stock trades at about a fifth of its listing price.

GENXAI.why: Below the ₹116 issue price: listed 12 June 2026 at ₹92.80 (a 20% discount) despite a 15.9x subscribed IPO, with the pre-IPO valuation (about ₹208 crore) and a sharp profit jump drawing scrutiny. It traded near ₹80 in August (52-week range ₹66.70-116). FY26 revenue rose 208% to ₹89 crore and profit 164% to ₹17.3 crore; EBITDA margin about 29.5%. It has a long association with Anaplan.
GENXAI.outlook: No analyst forecast or guidance found. Automated ratings: low on growth, high on valuation; technical signals bearish. The proceeds fund working capital, debt repayment and new product capex.

KRATIKAL.why: Up about 16% on the ₹135 issue price after listing 7 July 2026 at ₹192 (+42%) on a 205x subscribed IPO; it has since faded to about ₹160 (52-week range ₹153-199). FY26 total income rose to ₹36.9 crore from ₹21.1 crore and profit to ₹6.1 crore from ₹3.8 crore. It sells AI-driven cybersecurity SaaS and consulting; IPO money supports entry into the US and Middle East.
KRATIKAL.outlook: No analyst target or guidance found. The second half of the anchor lock-in ends 30 October 2026, a possible selling point. P/E about 31 and price-to-book 2.7 per one source (another shows 15x).

ENS.why: Up about 10% on the ₹92 issue price, trading about ₹102-105 after listing on BSE SME on 21 August 2026 (52-week range ₹95.76-110.64). Subscription was weak at one point (0.59x before close). FY26 revenue was about ₹51.4 crore with profit about ₹8.4 crore. It provides digital commerce enablement and software, and the issue was entirely fresh shares.
ENS.outlook: No analyst forecast, results or guidance found after listing. Proceeds fund product upgrades, hiring, IT infrastructure and debt repayment. Market cap about ₹137-139 crore.

BMISL.why: Listed flat at ₹110 on NSE SME on 5 October 2026 (IPO subscribed 103x) and rose to about ₹115.50 intraday on day one. Reported FY26 revenue ₹64.0 crore (₹50.8 crore a year earlier) and profit ₹10.2 crore (₹5.8 crore), from one unverified source. The fresh issue was ₹37.4 crore plus a ₹5.0 crore sale; promoters hold about 73%.
BMISL.outlook: No analyst forecast or post-listing results found. Lock-in ends for 50% of shares on 30 October 2026 and the rest on 29 December 2026. It is an IT and digital infrastructure firm; a newly listed SME stock trades thinly.

EIMS.why: Listed 8 October 2026 at ₹126 on BSE SME, a 48% premium to the ₹85 issue price, on an IPO subscribed 206-294x; it closed day one at ₹119.70. The ₹48.5 crore issue was ₹39.1 crore fresh plus a ₹9.4 crore sale. The listing summary warned profit and cash flow could be sensitive to operating and employee costs.
EIMS.outlook: No analyst forecast or post-listing results found. Market cap by my estimate: about ₹184 crore at the issue price and about ₹259 crore at the first close (2.16 crore post-issue shares). Newly listed SME stocks are volatile and thinly traded.

DSL.why: Below the ₹111 issue price: it listed flat on 8 October 2026 (₹110-111) on a weak 1.38x subscribed IPO (retail 0.81x) and closed day one at ₹104.80. ROE 33%, ROCE 42%, PAT margin 8.8% per the IPO profile; P/E about 9.6. It sells business messaging over SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice.
DSL.outlook: No analyst targets or post-listing results found. Simply Wall St scores valuation 2/6 and future growth 0/6 and flags illiquidity. Market cap about ₹230-270 crore.
